test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A serpent having many heads in Greek mythology
solution: The correct answer is: **Hydra**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The word **"Hydra"** refers to a serpent-like creature in Greek mythology that has multiple heads. If one head is cut off, two more grow in its place. (हाइड्रा - एक बहु-मस्तिष्क वाला सांप, ग्रीक पौराणिक कथाओं में) • **Example:** In Greek mythology, Hercules fought the nine-headed Hydra as part of his Twelve Labors. • **"Hydra"** symbolizes a formidable challenge or problem that multiplies when attempts are made to resolve it. (हाइड्रा - एक ऐसी समस्या जो प्रयासों के बावजूद बढ़ती जाती है) • **Example:** Corruption in the organization turned out to be a Hydra-like issue; every solution seemed to create more problems. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Hydra**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: __ • **Python** (पाइथन): A large non-venomous snake found in tropical and subtropical regions. It is unrelated to Hydra in mythology. • **Example:** The python coiled itself around the tree branch, basking in the sun. • **Cobra** (कोबरा): A venomous snake known for its hood, often found in Asia and Africa. It does not have multiple heads. • **Example:** The cobra raised its hood as a warning when it felt threatened. • **Eopsin** (एओप्सिन): A deity or mythical figure in Korean folklore associated with wealth and prosperity, not related to serpents. • **Example:** Eopsin is often depicted as a woman with a snake tail, symbolizing abundance. 13c:T8a7, The correct answer is **1.4%**__.
